summary: The human-readable recall block must emit code_info in full as a wrapped Lots/Expiry line; a regen must not drop the field or clip it to a fixed width.
reason: openFDA enforcement records carry the recalled lot numbers and expiry dates in code_info, and the generated recallRecord struct omitted the field entirely, so it never reached human-readable output. Measured over 100 live records the value runs median 50 / p90 261 / max 829 characters, so the clip(_, 100) treatment the prose fields use would lose data in roughly 22% of records. Unlike Product and Reason, code_info is identifying data rather than description: a partial lot number is not partially useful, and a fragment still reads as a valid lot. The value is therefore word-wrapped to the block's existing label column and never split mid-token. Rendering was extracted from runRecallSearch into printRecallRecord so the decode-to-output path is testable without a live API call; the fmt.Fprintf calls moved verbatim.
validated_outcome: go test ./internal/cli passes, including a round-trip test that decodes a raw openFDA payload through enforcementEnvelope and asserts every token of code_info survives into the rendered Lots/Expiry line at the block's indent.
